_column_contract: Summit's cover box runs Current | Last(=Previous, 2024 sheet) | Cumulative — the REVERSE of the parsed cities' sheet. All three columns are captured VERBATIM and LABELLED here; the builder promotes one per the rule documented in CLAUDE.md. "" = the cell was EMPTY (or a slashed-zero / dash nil mark) on the form; null = a value is present but ILLEGIBLE and was never guessed.

_meta_itemized.wave: itemized-vision(claude-opus-5; 2026-08-14 summit scan tranche, Phase B)

contributions.detail: exact, and confirmed three ways. The 30 rows sum to 3,770.00 = the module's stated total = the sum of the page's two printed boxes = the filer's own pencilled margin total '3770.='. Better still, the split is exact on BOTH sides independently: the thirteen rows above $50 sum to 3,085.00 (the '>$50' box to the cent) and the seventeen rows of $50 or less sum to 685.00 (the '<=$50' box to the cent). So this is a THIRD filing in this chunk where the <=$50 aggregate is itemized rather than merely totalled - and the first where the two classes are INTERLEAVED on one sheet rather than split across two. There is no structural residual at all. Specimen row 'Jon and Jane Doe $435.00' dropped; including it would give 4,205.00 and no box would close. No in-kind schedule exists on this filing. Two rows are declared ANONYMOUS CASH by the filer ('cash', 'cash - unknown', address 'Unknown') totalling $70.00 - honest anonymity on the face of the form, not missing data.

expenditures.detail: DELTA of $232.80, and it is a LEGIBILITY gap, NOT filer arithmetic and NOT a missing row. All 31 rows are transcribed; 26 carry an amount and those 26 sum to 7,076.94. FIVE amount cells - rows 5 (Walmart), 6 (Kamas Foodtown), 16 (a row whose date and vendor are also gone), 17 (Staples) and 22 (Costco) - are written in a hard pencil that the county's 300 ppi grayscale scan preserved only as ghost dots. Each was escalated to a tight cell crop at 1200 dpi and then to a contrast-stretched crop at the scan's own native resolution; neither resolves them beyond a leading digit. 7,309.74 - 7,076.94 = 232.80 is therefore exactly the sum of those five cells, which is a useful fact about the document but does NOT let any single one be recovered: one equation, five unknowns. They are stored BLANK with needs_review=1 rather than apportioned, and the rows are kept rather than dropped so the ledger's line count stays truthful. Specimen row 'Name of Business / Campaign signs and flyers / $512.00' dropped: including it would give 7,588.94 against a printed 7,309.74.

_meta_itemized.page_gates: Three pages: p1 cover (already transcribed), p2 ITEMIZED CONTRIBUTION REPORT, p3 ITEMIZED EXPENSE REPORT. Both are HARD-PENCIL handwriting on a photocopy and are the faintest sheets in this chunk; the county's OCR layer is pure noise on them (draft.py returns '1Vcq.T' for the expense total box), so nothing here comes from text. CONTRIBUTION GATE - AND IT IS A TRIPLE GATE, which is why every amount on p2 can be treated as confirmed: p2 prints '>$50 $3,085.00' and '<=$50 $685.00'; the filer ALSO pencilled his column total '3770.=' in the right margin beside the last row. The 30 rows sum to 3,770.00; splitting them by size, the thirteen rows over $50 sum to EXACTLY 3,085.00 and the seventeen rows of $50 or less sum to EXACTLY 685.00. Two independent partial sums closing to the cent over 30 handwritten rows is a far stronger check than one total, and it validates the amount column outright. 3,085.00 + 685.00 = 3,770.00 = the module's stated contribution total. EXPENSE GATE: p3 prints '7309.74' in its total box and the filer wrote the same figure again below the table. The 26 legible rows sum to 7,076.94; the 232.80 difference is exactly the five cells that are ILLEGIBLE (see recon.expenditures). Specimen rows dropped from both pages.

geometry.basis: rule-detection row banding (rowbands.py) on the page's own printed grid; box spans the full table width of the row

_meta_itemized.notes: Amy Yost, County Treasurer, 2014 Pre-Election. split50 form; both ledgers handwritten in hard pencil and photocopied before scanning. This filing spent $7,309.74 against $3,770.00 raised and closed $3,539.74 IN THE RED - the cover prints the balance in accountants' parentheses, '(3539.74)', which is why the module's stated balance is negative. SOURCE PROPERTIES WORTH RECORDING: (1) THE <=$50 CLASS IS ITEMIZED INTERLEAVED WITH THE >$50 CLASS ON A SINGLE SHEET. Hendricksen (1082/1246) itemized his small donors on a second sheet he hand-headed '$50.00 & less'; Yost simply listed everyone in date order and let the two printed boxes carry the split. Both boxes still close to the cent. Together these make the '>$50 only' expectation a DEFAULT, not a rule - three of the seven filings in this chunk itemize the aggregate. (2) THE FILER PENCILLED HER OWN COLUMN TOTAL IN THE MARGIN ('3770.=' beside the last contribution row). It is not a form field and is not published as one, but it is a third independent check on the column and it agrees. (3) TWO CONTRIBUTIONS ARE DECLARED ANONYMOUS ON THE FACE OF THE FORM - donor 'cash' and 'cash - unknown', address cell 'Unknown', zip blank, $50.00 and $20.00. Blank city/state on those rows means the filer said she did not know, which is a different fact from a cell she left empty and from a county redaction; the row notes say which. (4) DITTO MARKS ARE USED AS DATA in four places - a repeated address (Kristen Brown), a repeated name AND address (the $1,000 SC Republicans row), a repeated vendor and purpose (the second Post office stamps row) and a repeated purpose fragment (the second Kamas Foodtown row). A ditto mark is the filer STATING identity with the row above, so it is resolved to that value and the note records that the cell itself holds only the mark. Nothing is carried across a page break. (5) FIVE AMOUNT CELLS AND TWO DATE CELLS ARE GENUINELY ILLEGIBLE, and one whole expense row is a ghost (date, vendor and amount all gone, only '... Supplies' readable in the purpose cell). They are blank + needs_review, never reconstructed - see recon.expenditures for why the residual cannot apportion them. (6) A CANDIDATE IN THIS SAME CORPUS IS A DONOR HERE: Tal Adair, whose own 2016 filings are 4020 and 4278, gave $200. And the second-largest individual gift, $250 from Ryan Yost, shares the candidate's surname. Neither relationship is asserted in the data. (7) THREE ROWS ARE UNDATED (the first three contributions), and the expense ledger is not in date order, ending with a 07-07-14 row written with leading zeros. All kept as filed. PRIVACY: p2 prints a full Mailing Address and Zipcode column; every street address and PO box was discarded AT READ TIME and none appears in this record. donor_city / donor_state only, read from the address cell and NEVER from the zip - which matters on this filing, where Gregory Iverson's row pairs the town 'Peoa' with a Kamas zip (84036) and the pairing is retained as filed. Four rows print a town but no state token, so their donor_state is honestly blank. Nothing here is redacted by the county. GEOMETRY: both sides use DECLARED frames (force_declared). p2's rule detection is usable but its vertical rules stop at 78.1%, and p3's stop at 39.1% - i.e. a MEASURED box on p3 would cover only the Date and Vendor columns and would not show the amount, which is the whole point of the crop. Both grids were therefore measured on the RAW page in a narrow x-slice (which removes the deskewer's rotation) and declared: contributions x=9.52 y0=24.184 pitch=1.84283 w=78.81, expenditures x=9.24 y0=24.191 pitch=1.85429 w=79.0. Band 1 is the dropped specimen row on both pages, so data rows run 2..31 and 2..32. Validated by four probe crops - p2 band 2 (Paul Kunz / Kamas / 50.00), p2 band 31 (Deborah Lambert / 50.00), p3 band 2 (Summit County Clerk / Filing Fee / 781.03) and p3 band 32 (Oriental Trading / 67.50) - each reproducing donor/vendor AND amount.
